What we liked about the Wavytalk 1875W

1. 32,950 ratings is the most informative sample in this price range. Whatever the rating is, it is not a fluke of a small sample. When 32,950 Canadian buyers land on 4.3★, that number is stable and you can rely on what it says Amazon.ca data.

2. The listing is brand-operated. The Buy Box is held by wavytalk CA with a single seller and no competing resellers. Warranty and service complaints are the second-largest cluster in our dataset at 610 negative mentions and 81% negative, largely driven by reseller listings where nobody owns the claim. This listing avoids that entirely, and at about C$40 that is unusual (Amazon.ca data, review analysis).

3. A diffuser is included at about C$40. That makes it one of the cheapest routes to a diffuser in Canada. Attachment security is the most common curly-hair complaint in our data at 186 mentions and 57% negative, so a diffuser matched to the dryer holds better than a universal aftermarket part Review analysis.

4. It is sold in genuinely high volume. Roughly 2,948 units a month at BSR #3, with a 4.7-year track record. This is not a listing that appeared last month Amazon.ca data.

5. It is claimed to be ionic. Ionic has the best feature record in our entire dataset at 219 mentions and only 17% negative — though we could not verify the specification beyond the listing claim (manufacturer claim, review analysis).

What we didn’t like about the Wavytalk 1875W

1. 4.3★ is the lowest rating of any model we recommend. Against 4.6★ for the Laifen Air Diffuser and Dreame Pocket Pro, and 4.5★ for the Laifen Air and SE Lite. A 0.2–0.3 star gap sustained across 32,950 ratings is a real difference, not statistical noise Amazon.ca data. We cannot isolate the cause from our data and we will not guess at one.

2. It is a 1875W conventional design, not brushless. It relies more on heat than on airflow. That is the wrong approach for thick or long hair, where airflow is what shortens drying time — airflow was the most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,585 mentions, and complaints run one way: too weak, never too powerful (manufacturer claim, review analysis).

3. It is the wrong design for heat-sensitive hair. Heat and temperature generated 1,093 mentions with 54% negative in our data, and the pattern is scorching rather than slow drying Review analysis. A heat-first dryer is a poor match if that is your concern.

4. Budget price band, where complaints are three times as common. Under C$50, our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate across 3,259 reviews, against 9.6% over C$120 across 334. The Wavytalk sits in the high-complaint band Review analysis.

5. We have not measured it. No airflow, noise, weight or dry time. Every measured row in this review reads “not yet tested,” which applies to every dryer we cover — see how we test.

Wavytalk 1875W performance and heat

What we can say. The Wavytalk is a conventional 1875W dryer, which means the heating element does more of the work than the motor. High-speed brushless dryers invert that — they move a large volume of air at lower temperature Manufacturer claim.

Why the distinction matters for your hair type. Drying is fundamentally a water-removal problem, and moving air removes water faster than raising its temperature does. That is why airflow dominates our complaint data and why reviewers with thick hair describe conventional dryers as inadequate rather than as too hot.

For which hair types the Wavytalk works. Fine to medium hair that is not heat-sensitive, and shorter hair where the total drying time is small. It includes a diffuser, so it is usable on wavy hair if the diffuser holds.

For which it does not. Thick, coarse or long hair, where you want airflow. And heat-sensitive, damaged or colour-treated hair, where a heat-first design works against you. Our thick hair guide and fine hair guide cover what to look for instead.

What we cannot say. How hot it actually runs, how fast it dries, or how it compares on airflow to any specific competitor. We have not measured any of it, and we do not publish estimates.

Who should buy the Wavytalk 1875W

Buy it if:

  • Your budget is genuinely under C$45 and you want a diffuser included
  • Your hair is fine to medium, not heat-sensitive, and not especially long
  • You value a brand-operated listing with one seller at a budget price
  • You want the reassurance of a 32,950-rating sample rather than a new listing

Do not buy it if:

  • Your hair is thick or long — you want airflow, and this is a heat-first design
  • Your hair is heat-sensitive, damaged or colour-treated
  • You want the highest rating for the money — the Laifen Air Diffuser is C$60 more at 4.6★
  • You need dual voltage for travel

Wavytalk hair dryer FAQ

Is Wavytalk a good hair dryer brand? It has the second-largest review base in the entire Canadian category at 32,950 ratings, and the listing is brand-operated rather than resold. But it also carries the lowest rating of any model we recommend at 4.3 stars. Large sample and high rating are not the same thing, and both facts belong in the decision.

Why is the Wavytalk rating lower than cheaper alternatives? We cannot isolate the cause from our data, and we will not guess. What we can report is the gap: 4.3 stars against 4.6 for the Laifen Air Diffuser and Dreame Pocket Pro, and 4.5 for the Laifen Air and SE Lite. A 0.2 to 0.3 star gap across 32,950 ratings is a meaningful difference, not noise.

Does the Wavytalk hair dryer include a diffuser? Yes, a diffuser is included, which makes it one of the cheapest ways to get one. Attachment security is the most common curly-hair complaint in our data at 186 mentions and 57% negative, so check the fit when it arrives and return it inside the return window if it does not hold.

Is Wavytalk a high-speed brushless hair dryer? No. It is a 1875W conventional design, which means it relies more on heat than on airflow. That matters if your hair is thick or long, where airflow is what actually shortens drying time. It is also the wrong approach for heat-sensitive or fine hair.

Who sells the Wavytalk hair dryer in Canada? The listing is brand-operated, with the Buy Box held by wavytalk CA and a single seller. That is a better warranty structure than a listing with several competing resellers and a third-party Buy Box, and it is the same structure Laifen, Dreame, Aina and Dyson use.

Is Wavytalk good for curly hair? It is usable, because it includes a diffuser and it is cheap. But it is a heat-first conventional dryer rather than a high-airflow lower-heat design, and heat is the mechanism behind the frizz complaints in our data. If your curls are heat-sensitive, spend the extra on the Laifen Air Diffuser.

Our verdict on the Wavytalk 1875W

Good budget structure, mediocre rating — and both halves are true.

The Wavytalk 1875W at about C$40 has the second-largest review base in Canada at 32,950 ratings, a brand-operated listing with a single seller, a diffuser included, and roughly 2,948 units a month at BSR #3. For a budget buyer whose hair is fine to medium and not heat-sensitive, that is a defensible purchase, and the brand-operated listing is a genuine advantage over every other budget option we cover.

But 4.3★ is the lowest rating of any model we recommend, and it is sustained across a very large sample. We cannot tell you why from our data, and we will not invent an explanation.

If you can stretch to about C$100, the Laifen Air Diffuser rates 4.6★ and sits in the price band where complaint rates fall from 30.3% to 9.6%. That C$60 buys a materially better position on both measures — and if you want to see how that trade plays out across the whole category, our best hair dryers guide ranks them side by side.
